title: Saturation-aware microbatch admission heuristic with KV-headroom accounting
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem summary:

Under sustained high QPS (1000-5k RPS per model shard) we've observed cascaded failures driven by continuous batching + aggressive KV cache residency. The serving runtime currently uses a fixed microbatch admission threshold (microbatch_target_size) and a simple GPU headroom check. When request size or token variance increases, the runtime overpacks microbatches which causes: (1) KV cache eviction spikes, (2) transient GPU memory pressure leading to OOM throttles or retries, and (3) amplified p95/p99 tail latency due to long-running big microbatches.

Goal:
Design and implement a saturation-aware admission controller that dynamically adjusts microbatch thresholds and applies graduated backpressure based on three signals: observed KV cache hit ratio, per-GPU reserved-slab headroom (in tokens/bytes), and latency percentiles. The goal is to maintain latency SLOs (p95 under target), avoid OOMs, and minimize reject/429s while preserving throughput and cost efficiency.

High-level approach / heuristics:
1) Headroom accounting: track a moving-window estimate of effective available GPU memory dedicated to KV cache + transient activations. Convert to an approximate token-headroom using model-specific token->bytes mapping. Use this to compute an upper-bound on safe simultaneous generated tokens.

2) Adaptive microbatch cap: set microbatch_cap = clamp(floor(headroom_tokens / avg_tokens_per_request), min_mb, max_mb). min_mb and max_mb are conservative limits (e.g., 1 and 128) configurable per-model. This ensures we don't build batches larger than what the current memory headroom can safely execute.

3) Soft vs hard admission gates:
   - Soft gate: when KV-hit_ratio drops below threshold_1 or p95 latency creeps above soft_p95, start probabilistic shedding of low-priority requests (sample-based rejection) and reduce microbatch_cap by a fraction (e.g., 25%).
   - Hard gate: when headroom_tokens < hard_min_tokens OR GPU transient allocations exceed hard_utilization (e.g., 92%), reject to caller with explicit backpressure response (429 + Retry-After) or fast-fail with graceful fallback route to a cheaper model variant.

4) Priority-aware shedding: requests carry priority metadata (system, user-high, user-low). Shedding should prefer user-low and best-effort routes. For hosted API customers without explicit priority, default to customer-tier mapping (free->lower).

5) KV-aware admission scoring: maintain request-level expected-kv-reads estimate (from prompt fingerprinting and cached prefix length). Higher expected kv read estimates reduce admission probability when KV-hit_ratio is low.

6) Rate-limit integration: admission controller should coordinate with the rate-limiter to avoid double counting. Use admission decisions as part of token accounting for quota usage analytics.

Implementation notes and data structures (runtime changes):
- New controller module `admission/saturation_controller` with these inputs: node_metrics (gpu_mem_free, slab_reserved, slab_total), kv_metrics (hit_ratio, cardinality_est), request_stats (avg_tokens, 95th_tokens, pri), and queue_length.
- Lightweight token-headroom estimator: headroom_tokens = floor((slab_reserved - kv_expected_bytes) / avg_bytes_per_token). kv_expected_bytes estimated via rolling avg of per-request KV bytes touched.
- Persist microbatch_cap per-shard with TTL (10s) to avoid oscillations. Add hysteresis with exponential backoff on increases and immediate clamp down on decreases.
- Add telemetry: admission_decision, reason_code, microbatch_cap, headroom_tokens, kv_hit_ratio, p95_latency at 1s resolution to our tracing pipeline.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics:
- No GPU OOMs observed in canary group (0 OOMs over 24h under synthetic 3k RPS workload)
- p95 latency reduction or stability: p95 should not exceed baseline+10% during sustained load and should improve in >50% of experiment windows where KV hit ratio is poor (<70%).
- Reject rate under backpressure should be <3% for user-high and <10% for user-low in high load scenarios.
- Cost impact: throughput normalized per-GPU should remain within -5%/+10% of baseline (acceptable variance).

Experiment plan (canary -> ramp -> global):
- Phase A (lab): run synthetic workload (mixture of short/long prompts, token variance) on a dedicated dev shard, compare current vs saturation-controller for 12h. Metrics: OOM count, p95/p99, KV hit ratio, effective throughput.
- Phase B (canary): deploy to 5% of production traffic for a small subset of model families (Llama2-13B variants + quantized small models) with conservative min_mb and soft thresholds. Collect 48h.
- Phase C (ramp): if canary stable, increase to 25% and enable priority-aware shedding. 72h monitoring.
- Phase D: full rollout behind runtime-1.22 with opt-out flag for critical enterprise customers until validated.

Fallbacks and compatibility:
- Admission controller is purely local and can be disabled via runtime flag. When disabled, system falls back to current fixed microbatch target.
- Provide a customer telem label (admission_mode=legacy|saturation) so Console dashboards can filter.

Open design trade-offs and risks:
- Estimating kv_expected_bytes adds estimation error; misestimation could be conservative (lower microbatch_cap) reducing throughput. We'll tune decay windows.
- Oscillation risk: too-aggressive increases can cause ping-pong. Mitigate with TTL and hysteresis.
- Complexity for multi-tenant GPU: decisions are per-shard; cross-tenant fairness requires future global allocator changes.

comments: 2026-02-12 — Priya Nair: Kicked off design doc. Spiked two prototypes for token-headroom estimator (one using slab bytes, one using activation-window sampling). Slab-based was simpler and near-term feasible.

2026-02-20 — Miguel Torres: Implemented initial admission module; added microbatch_cap TTL and hysteresis. Unit tests passing locally. Prototype PR opened (4869). Observed ~12% throughput drop in synthetic worst-case but p95 improved by 28% and OOMs eliminated in lab run.

2026-02-24 — Rajiv Menon: Ran perf harness (perf-2026-02-18-01). Baseline vs controller: OOMs 3->0 over 6h; p95 460ms->330ms on mixed prompt workload at 2.5k RPS. KV hit ratio was main driver; when hit_ratio < 65% controller throttled more aggressively.

2026-03-02 — Kala Winston: Dashboard PR (observability #954) includes new panels for microbatch_cap and admission_reason. Console owners requested ability to group by customer_tier — added as follow-up task.

2026-03-08 — Miguel Torres: Canary started on 5% traffic for select models. Initial 12h window: one enterprise tenant reported increased rejects; flagged and we enabled opt-out for their dedicated shards. Investigating priority mapping defaults.

2026-03-13 — Priya Nair: Decided to add an extra safety-hold: when repeating hard gates happen >3 times within 60s, we auto-scale shard with burst capacity (if available) before escalating to global rejects. Added to rollout tasks.
